Risk officer view: I'd refuse any size, so the desk should skip this one.

The brief is mixed. The curve shows no airdrop dump and a reasonable top-3 share (8.7%), but the first two minutes after graduation show a sell-to-buy ratio of 0.95, a launch bot present, and a bundle share of 24.5%. The last 15 minutes show net flow of only +30 SOL on about 1,027 SOL of buying, with more sellers (1,766) than buyers would suggest churn. It is already 30% off its 30-minute high, and the 2.2x return means late entrants are underwater on the pullback. Pool depth of 157 SOL is thin for a $20 ticket once the 1.4-5.1% round-trip cost is added.

Nothing here clears the bar for an organic-coin edge against a base rate of roughly -20% per trade. Skip.
memos.scout:
The strongest case for buying is the last-15-minute tape: 2,203 buyers putting in 1,026 SOL against 996 SOL of sells, a net inflow of about 30 SOL with the price up 12%. That is real two-sided trading, not a single operator in and out. The curve is also reasonably distributed: top-3 holders hold about 8.7%, and the first two minutes after graduation show a top-5 buyer share of only 8.4%, with the sell-to-buy ratio at 0.95, so early wallets did not dump the coin. It is classified ORGANIC with no airdrop dump, and the coin is still alive at 30 minutes with a 2.2x return.

The case is weakened by a 30% drawdown from the 30-minute high and by a bundle share of 24.5% on the curve, which suggests some coordinated early buying. Net flow over the last 15 minutes is only slightly positive against a round-trip cost of 1.4-5.1% on a pool of about 157 SOL. This is a thin edge on a coin that has already run and is retracing, so I'd call it a marginal buy at best, and the desk should treat it as a low-conviction ticket if it takes one at all.
memos.skeptic:
The most likely loss path is distribution into the late-stage tape. The coin is up 218% over 30 minutes but has already drawn down 30% from its high, and the last 15 minutes show $247.9K of volume with sell SOL (996.4) nearly matching buy SOL (1,026.7) and net flow only +30 SOL. Sellers (1,766) outnumber the buyer count that drove the move, and the sell-to-buy ratio at graduation was 0.945, so early buyers are exiting into new demand.

Insider overhang is also visible: bundled wallets hold a 24.5% curve share and the graduation completer holds 24.5%. Against a $20 ticket and 1.4-5.1% round-trip costs, a 30% drawdown from peak leaves little room for a further dip to hit. Pool depth of 157 SOL means exits get thinner if sellers accelerate.

Verdict: skip.
